[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Distributed Training with MirroredStrategy and MultiWorkerMirroredStrategy in TensorFlow"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Scaling deep learning models across multiple GPUs and machines is essential for reducing training times on large datasets. TensorFlow provides the Distribution Strategy API to facilitate this with minimal code changes. This tutorial covers MirroredStrategy for single-machine, multi-GPU training, and MultiWorkerMirroredStrategy for distributed training across multiple compute nodes."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"Prerequisites and Setup"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before starting, ensure you have TensorFlow installed. You can verify your GPU availability using the following Python snippet."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"import tensorflow as tf
print("TensorFlow version:", tf.__version__)
print("Num GPUs Available: ", len(tf.config.list_physical_devices('GPU')))"},{"order":6,"type":"heading","text":"Understanding MirroredStrategy"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"tf.distribute.MirroredStrategy implements synchronous distributed training on multiple GPUs on a single machine. It creates copies (mirrors) of all variables on each of the available GPUs. Here is how it operates:"},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Data is evenly distributed across the available GPUs (data parallelism)."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Each GPU computes the gradients for its slice of the input data."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Gradients are all-reduced across all GPUs, meaning they are averaged so every GPU has the exact same gradient update."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Model variables are updated synchronously across all replicas."},{"order":12,"type":"heading","text":"Implementing MirroredStrategy"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"To use MirroredStrategy, instantiate the strategy object and create your model inside the strategy.scope() context manager. This ensures that all variables are created as mirrored variables."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"import tensorflow as tf

# Initialize the strategy
strategy = tf.distribute.MirroredStrategy()
print('Number of devices: {}'.format(strategy.num_replicas_in_sync))

# Open the strategy scope to build and compile the model
with strategy.scope():
    model = tf.keras.Sequential([
        tf.keras.layers.Dense(128, activation='relu', input_shape=(784,)),
        tf.keras.layers.Dropout(0.2),
        tf.keras.layers.Dense(10, activation='softmax')
    ])
    
    model.compile(
        loss='sparse_categorical_crossentropy',
        optimizer='adam',
        metrics=['accuracy']
    )"},{"order":15,"type":"heading","text":"Understanding MultiWorkerMirroredStrategy"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"When scaling beyond a single machine, tf.distribute.MultiWorkerMirroredStrategy is used. It extends MirroredStrategy to span across multiple machines (workers), each potentially having multiple GPUs. It uses synchronous all-reduce communication, typically backed by NCCL or Ring-allreduce."},{"order":17,"type":"heading","text":"Configuring Cluster Environment for MultiWorkerMirroredStrategy"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"MultiWorkerMirroredStrategy relies on the TF_CONFIG environment variable to understand the cluster topology, including the addresses and ports of all workers, and the current worker's index."},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"import os
import json

# Example TF_CONFIG for a 2-node cluster
os.environ['TF_CONFIG'] = json.dumps({
    'cluster': {
        'worker': ['host1:12345', 'host2:12345']
    },
    'task': {'type': 'worker', 'index': 0}
})"},{"order":20,"type":"heading","text":"Implementing MultiWorkerMirroredStrategy"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"The code structure for MultiWorkerMirroredStrategy is very similar to MirroredStrategy. The strategy automatically reads TF_CONFIG to configure the communication channels."},{"order":22,"type":"code","text":"import tensorflow as tf

# Initialize the multi-worker strategy
strategy = tf.distribute.MultiWorkerMirroredStrategy()

with strategy.scope():
    # Define model inside scope
    multi_worker_model = tf.keras.Sequential([
        tf.keras.layers.Dense(256, activation='relu', input_shape=(784,)),
        tf.keras.layers.Dense(10, activation='softmax')
    ])
    
    multi_worker_model.compile(
        loss='sparse_categorical_crossentropy',
        optimizer='adam',
        metrics=['accuracy']
    )"},{"order":23,"type":"heading","text":"Dataset Batching and Distributed Input"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"When training with distribution strategies, the global batch size must be scaled appropriately. Each step processes a batch of data split across the replicas. The global batch size is typically multiplied by the number of replicas."},{"order":25,"type":"code","text":"BUFFER_SIZE = 10000
BATCH_SIZE_PER_REPLICA = 64
GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE = BATCH_SIZE_PER_REPLICA * strategy.num_replicas_in_sync

# Load and preprocess dataset
mnist = tf.keras.datasets.mnist
(x_train, y_train), (x_test, y_test) = mnist.load_data()
x_train = x_train.reshape(60000, 784).astype('float32') / 255.0

train_dataset = tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices((x_train, y_train))
train_dataset = train_dataset.shuffle(BUFFER_SIZE).batch(GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE)"},{"order":26,"type":"heading","text":"Best Practices and Summary"},{"order":27,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always instantiate models and optimizers inside the strategy.scope() block to ensure correct variable placement."},{"order":28,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Scale your batch size linearly with the number of replicas to maintain training dynamics."},{"order":29,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use MirroredStrategy for single nodes with multiple GPUs, and transition to MultiWorkerMirroredStrategy when scaling horizontally across multiple physical servers."}]
